name: Sammamish
seo_title: 2 Christmas Events for Kids in Sammamish, WA 2026
seo_desc: 2 Christmas events for kids in Sammamish, WA, 1 free: Holidays in Sammamish with the Sammamish Symphony and more.
lede: Sammamish keeps Christmas cozy and close to home, with a free Frosty Fest from the city's parks department and a holiday concert from the hometown symphony.
celebrates: Sammamish Parks and Recreation hosts Frosty Fest each December, a free family evening with hot cocoa, cookies and crafts that has moved between City Hall and other city buildings over the years. The Sammamish Symphony Orchestra, which calls itself classical music for the Eastside, plays a holiday concert at the Eastlake Performing Arts Center with seasonal favorites, movie music and Hansel and Gretel, and youth tickets for ages 5 to 18 are free. For bigger outings, families head down the plateau to Issaquah and Redmond, where light displays, trolley rides and reindeer fill the season.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Sammamish hosted Frosty Fest on Wednesday, December 17, from 4 to 7 pm at City Hall. The city invited community members to enjoy complimentary cocoa, coffee, tea and desserts inside the building, with the Five Hooks food truck parked on site. The city described it as a free, family friendly event and a festive chance for residents to gather and celebrate the season together before the winter break.
facts: Sammamish is one of the newest cities in King County. It formally incorporated on August 31, 1999, after a decade of debate, and residents tossed around names like Monohon, Inglewood, Sahalee and even Heaven before Sammamish won. The plateau's first permanent settler, Martin Monohon, arrived in 1877. By 1911 the mill town of Monohon on Lake Sammamish had 300 people, its own water system, a railroad depot and a 20 room hotel.
trains: Trains built the first town here. In 1889 the Seattle, Lake Shore and Eastern Railroad finished a track along the eastern shore of Lake Sammamish, and a mill opened at Monohon that November, giving the town its anchor for 36 years along with a railroad depot. Today the closest light rail is the Link 2 Line, which opened Marymoor Village and Downtown Redmond stations on May 10, 2025. The Issaquah Valley Trolley and the Northwest Railway Museum in Snoqualmie are short drives away.
train_links: A restored streetcar ride from the historic Issaquah Depot, run by Issaquah History Museums volunteers.

traditions: The city's free December family night, with cocoa, cookies and crafts, now with a Frozen movie night in pajamas.
The Sammamish Symphony Orchestra's December concert at the Eastlake Performing Arts Center.
The Sammamish Symphony made tickets free for ages 5 to 18, so a first concert costs nothing for kids.
Frosty Fest guests make a holiday ornament to take home.
kidfact: Before Sammamish picked its name in 1999, people suggested calling it Monohon, Inglewood, Sahalee and even Heaven.
faq: What is Frosty Fest in Sammamish?

Frosty Fest is the City of Sammamish's free winter family event, run by Sammamish Parks and Recreation. Past years offered complimentary cocoa, coffee, tea and desserts at City Hall. This year's edition is a Magical Movie in a Winter Wonderland at Building 120, with pajamas, popcorn, an ornament craft, Frozen character photos and Disney's Frozen.
Is there a holiday concert for kids in Sammamish?

Yes. The Sammamish Symphony Orchestra plays its Holidays in Sammamish concert each December at the Eastlake Performing Arts Center at Eastlake High School. The orchestra made youth tickets for ages 5 to 18 free, and adult tickets are $20, so it is an affordable first symphony for school age children.
When did Sammamish become a city?

Sammamish formally incorporated on August 31, 1999, after about a decade of debate and one failed incorporation vote. Its first census in 2000 counted 34,104 residents. Before then the plateau was unincorporated King County, with communities such as Monohon and Inglewood along the shore of Lake Sammamish.
Where is the nearest light rail to Sammamish?

The Link 2 Line ends in Redmond. Sound Transit opened Marymoor Village and Downtown Redmond stations on May 10, 2025, with a 1,400 space parking garage at Marymoor Village. From there trains run west through Redmond Technology Station and Bellevue, which makes a light rail ride an easy add on to a holiday outing.
